Geasey Trophy]] (2021, 2022) * [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] MVP ([[2022 Big East men's basketball tournament|2022]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Basketball at the Pan American Games|Pan American Games]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2019 Lima]]|[[United States men's national basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Collin Andrew Gillespie''' (born June 25, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]]. Gillespie was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East co-Player of the Year]] in 2021 and won it outright the following year. ==Early life== Gillespie grew up just outside Philadelphia and is the son of a police officer. He attended [[Archbishop Wood Catholic High School]], where he was coached by John Mosco. Gillespie had no Division I scholarship offers coming into his senior year, but received offers from [[Rider Broncs men's basketball|Rider]], [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]] and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] after strong play in a tournament.{{cite news|last1=Jensen|first1=Mike|title=Villanova freshman Collin Gillespie proving he belongs|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/collin-gillespie-villanova-basketball-freshman-season-archbishop-wood-20180202.html|access-date=May 6, 2018|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=February 2, 2018}} He scored 42 points in a regular-season win over [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School|Neumann Goretti]] featuring Kentucky recruit [[Quade Green]].{{cite news|last1=Moore|first1=Tom|title=Moore: Archbishop Wood grad Collin Gillespie can join select group with 2 Villanova wins|url=http://www.theintell.com/sports/20180327/moore-archbishop-wood-grad-collin-gillespie-can-join-select-group-with-2-villanova-wins|access-date=May 6, 2018|work=[[The Intelligencer (Doylestown, Pennsylvania)|The Intelligencer]]|date=March 28, 2018|archive-date=June 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628154732/http://www.theintell.com/sports/20180327/moore-archbishop-wood-grad-collin-gillespie-can-join-select-group-with-2-villanova-wins|url-status=dead}} As a senior, he led the team to a PIAA Class 5A state title in 2017.{{cite news|last1=Moore|first1=Tom|title=Freshman Collin Gillespie has given Villanova an unanticipated spark this season|url=http://www.mcall.com/sports/college/mc-spt-villanova-basketball-colline-gillespie-20180306-story.html|access-date=May 7, 2018|work=[[The Morning Call]]|date=March 6, 2018}} Gillespie averaged 24.1 points per game as a senior and was named Philadelphia Player of the Year by the [[Philadelphia Daily News]] as well as Catholic League Most Valuable Player. He signed a letter of intent with Villanova on April 14, 2017, joining Dhamir Cosby-Roundtree and [[Jermaine Samuels]] in the class of 2021.{{cite news|last1=Murphy|first1=Mike|title=Archbishop Wood basketball star Collin Gillespie signs with Villanova|url=http://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/ncaa/archbishop-wood-basketball-star-collin-gillespie-signs-villanova|access-date=May 6, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 14, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Collin Gillespie.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Gillespie in 2018]] Gillespie enrolled at Villanova in the fall of 2017, and he wanted to redshirt his freshman year at the school, but coach [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]] decided against doing it because Gillespie "was playing above his years." Soon breaking into the rotation, Gillespie scored in double figures in his second collegiate game, but he also had to learn to adjust to the quickness of the college game. Gillespie had to miss more than a month in December and January due to a fractured bone in his left hand sustained in a December 10 practice. However, he returned to action in a January 17 road win over [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. He provided quality minutes and had eight points including two three-pointers in a February 1 win over [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]] due to the absence of [[Phil Booth (basketball)|Phil Booth]] with a similar hand injury. Gillespie made his first start on February 10, in an 86–75 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]]. In the first round of the NCAA Tournament, Gillespie scored nine points and had a steal in a win versus [[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford]]. He had four points and five rebounds in the 79–62 [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|NCAA championship game]] win over [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]]. He averaged 4.3 points per game in 14.4 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=2 Collin Gillespie|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/collin_gillespie_1052385.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823050033/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/collin_gillespie_1052385.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 23, 2017|website=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|access-date=May 6, 2018}} Gillespie posted a 2.6-to-1 assist to turnover ratio, which Wright attributed to him thinking about his teammates and trying to make them better. Gillespie scored a season-high 30 points in a 77–65 win against Georgetown on February 3, 2019.{{cite news |title=Gillespie's career game carries No. 14 Villanova past Hoyas |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401083284 |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 3, 2019}} On March 9, he had 22 points in a 79–75 loss to [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite news |title=Seton Hall scores second big upset, stuns No. 23 Villanova |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401083336 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 9, 2019}} As a sophomore, Gillespie averaged 10.9 points per game.{{cite news |title=Breakdown: Purdue vs. Villanova |url=http://www.journalgazette.net/sports/colleges/purdue/20190323/breakdown-purdue-vs-villanova |access-date=March 29, 2019 |work=[[The Journal Gazette]] |date=March 23, 2019 |archive-date=March 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329234316/http://www.journalgazette.net/sports/colleges/purdue/20190323/breakdown-purdue-vs-villanova |url-status=dead }} Coming into his junior season, Gillespie broke his nose in practice, forcing him to wear a mask for several games.{{cite news |last1=Juliano |first1=Joe |title=Injuries are affecting Collin Gillespie's prep for start of Villanova's basketball season |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-point-guard-collin-gillespie-sidelined-broken-nose-wildcats-coach-jay-wright-20191024.html |access-date=December 1, 2019 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=October 24, 2019}} Gillespie had 27 points and six assists in an 87–78 loss to [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] in the championship game of the Myrtle Beach Classic. |url=https://villanova.com/news/2021/3/10/mens-basketball-gillespie-robinson-earl-among-3-big-east-players-of-the-year.aspx |website=[[Villanova Wildcats]] |access-date=December 4, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} He averaged 14 points and 4.6 assists per game. Gillespie decided to take advantage of the additional season of eligibility granted by the NCAA due to the COVID-19 pandemic.{{cite news |last1=Cobb |first1=David |title=Villanova's Collin Gillespie, Jermaine Samuels returning to Wildcats for 2021–22 college basketball season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-picks-schedule-predictions-for-alabama-vs-gonzaga-and-other-top-games-saturday/ |access-date=December 4, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=April 12, 2021}} On February 15, 2022, Gillespie scored a career-high 33 points despite playing on a swollen ankle in an 89–84 win at [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]].{{cite news |title=Gillespie nets 33, No. 10 Villanova beats No. 8 Friars 89–84 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401373591 |access-date=February 16, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 15, 2022}} He was named outright Big East Player of the Year for the 2021–22 season.{{cite news|last =Moore| first =Tom| title=Gillespie hopes he has 4 games left at Villanova |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/827715203 |newspaper=[[Courier-Post]] |location=[[Cherry Hill, New Jersey]] |date=March 24, 2022 |page= B4|via =Newspapers.com|accessdate = March 16, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Denver Nuggets / Grand Rapids Gold (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Gillespie signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=Nuggets Sign Collin Gillespie to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-collin-gillespie-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2022-07-13 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} Gillespie joined the Nuggets' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] team. In his Summer League debut, Gillespie scored 11 points, six rebounds, and four assists in a 78–85 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |title=Denver Nuggets 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612743/nuggets |access-date=2022-07-13 |website=www.nba.com}}{{Cite web |title=Denver Nuggets vs Minnesota Timberwolves Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/den-vs-min-1522200008/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-13 |website=www.nba.com}} In four Summer League games, he averaged 11.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=Nuggets two-way guard Collin Gillespie out indefinitely after fracturing leg |url=https://www.denverstiffs.com/platform/amp/2022/7/30/23285076/nuggets-two-way-guard-collin-gillespie-out-indefinitely-after-fracturing-leg |access-date=2022-07-30 |website=SB Nation |archive-date=2022-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730163458/https://www.denverstiffs.com/platform/amp/2022/7/30/23285076/nuggets-two-way-guard-collin-gillespie-out-indefinitely-after-fracturing-leg |url-status=dead }} On July 30, 2022, the Nuggets announced that Gillespie had undergone surgery for a lower leg fracture and that he would be out indefinitely. Gillespie ended his rookie season as an [[NBA champion]] when the Nuggets beat the [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2023 NBA Finals]], albeit without making his NBA debut. On July 18, 2023, Gillespie re-signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]] on another two-way contract.{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN GILLESPIE, HUFF AND KEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-gillespie-huff-and-key-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} ===Phoenix Suns (2024–present)=== ====2024–25 season==== On July 2, 2024, Gillespie signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN COLLIN GILLESPIE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-collin-gillespie-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}} Gillespie would make his Phoenix Suns debut on October 26, with the Suns winning 114–102 over the defending Western Conference champion [[2024–25 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] in Phoenix's home opener. Gillespie recorded a season-high 10 points on 4-of-6 shooting, including 2-for-3 from 3-point range, in the team's 23-point comeback win against the [[2024–25 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]] on March 4, 2025. His point total, along with three assists and two rebounds, came in 15 minutes of playing time during the third and fourth quarters.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-05 |title=Suns can't waste spark from Kevin Durant, Collin Gillespie |url=https://gophnx.com/suns-cant-waste-spark-kevin-durant-collin-gillespie-clippers-comeback-win/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=gophnx.com |language=en-US}} Gillespie's play style during the game drew comparisons to Suns great [[Steve Nash]].{{Cite web |last=Ronayne |first=Angelia |date=2025-03-05 |title=Suns Turn to Unlikely Hero in Fourth Quarter Comeback |url=https://lastwordonsports.com/basketball/2025/03/05/suns-unlikely-hero-collin-gillespie/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |website=Last Word On Basketball |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=NBA on TNT |date=March 4, 2025 |title="LOOKIN' LIKE STEVE NASH OUT HERE" |url=https://x.com/NBAonTNT/status/1897152861290877409 |access-date=March 5, 2025 |website=X.com}} Gillespie made his first career start on March 17 against the [[2024–25 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]], ending the game with three points on 1-of-4 shooting.{{Cite web|title=Suns' Collin Gillespie: Quiet in first career |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/06/suns-to-re-sign-collin-gillespie.html |access-date=July 2, 2025 |website=Hoops Rumors}} On November 21, Gillespie scored the game-winning jumper with 6.4 seconds left, Suns rally to stun Timberwolves 114-113 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401809795 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 5, 2026}} On February night, Suns outlast Blazers minus Booker, Green |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2026/02/03/suns-trail-blazers-score-game-updates-news/88348762007/ |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US}} On April 2, Gillespie set the franchise record for most made three-pointers in a season, surpassing [[Quentin Richardson]]'s previous record of 226 which was set during the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]].{{Cite web|title=Collin Gillespie breaks Suns' franchise record for most 3-pointers in a season|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/collin-gillespie-breaks-suns-franchise-record-for-most-3-pointers-in-a-season|access-date=June 21, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} During the 2025–26 season, Gillespie averaged career-highs in nearly every major statistical category, including points per game (12.7), minutes per game (28.5), assists per game (4.6), and games started (58). He helped the Suns clinch a 45–37 record and the eighth seed in the playoffs after a [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] win over the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]], a successful turnaround for the team after a 2024–25 season that saw them miss the playoffs. The Suns faced the reigning champion and top-seeded [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]] during their first-round series. On April 19, Gillespie made his playoff debut, recording eight points and two assists in a 119–84 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 25 AS REIGNING CHAMPION THUNDER OPEN PLAYOFFS WITH 119-84 WIN OVER SUNS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500141 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On April 27, he scored a playoff career-high 20 points in a 131–122 Game 4 loss, which effectively ended the Suns' season in a first-round playoff sweep.{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SCORES 31 AND THUNDER OUTLAST SUNS 131-122 TO CAP A 4-GAME SWEEP |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500144 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} ====2026–27 season==== On June 20, 2026, Gillespie re-signed with the Suns on a four-year, $48 million contract.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Gillespie returning to Suns on 4-year, $48 million deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49129656/sources-gillespie-returning-suns-4-year-48-million-deal|access-date=June 21, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==National team career== In the summer of 2019, Gillespie was a part of the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States National team]] who competed at the [[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|Pan American Games]] in Peru.
